priorStories.headline: Binance says $3 billion frozen after crypto theft
priorStories.body:
Binance said roughly $3 billion in assets affected by an estimated $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft disclosed Thursday had been frozen with help from blockchain partners. The exchange said it was beginning efforts to recover money for users.

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM assessed that a North Korean hacking unit was probably responsible.

priorStories.headline: DEA starts registering 900 medical-marijuana dispensaries
priorStories.body:
The Drug Enforcement Administration began issuing federal registrations to more than 900 state-licensed medical-marijuana dispensaries in Alabama, Florida, Mississippi, South Dakota, Texas, Virginia and West Virginia.

The registrations implement federal Schedule III controls for qualifying medical-marijuana activities. Recipients must comply with federal security, recordkeeping and inventory requirements.

priorStories.headline: Euro-area economy grows 0.4% in third quarter
priorStories.body:
The euro-area economy expanded 0.4% from the previous quarter, according to Eurostat’s preliminary estimate. Growth slowed from 0.6% in the second quarter but exceeded economists’ expectation of 0.2%.

Output across the 21 countries using the euro was 1.3% higher than a year earlier.

priorStories.headline: Judge blocks DOJ threats to election officials
priorStories.body:
A federal judge temporarily barred the Justice Department from threatening state and local election officials with prosecution for rejecting administration demands concerning alleged noncitizen voters.

The order also blocks demands to remove listed voters or reject or segregate their ballots during the midterm elections.

priorStories.headline: U.S. measles count reaches 4,852 cases
priorStories.body:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 4,852 measles cases through October 29, an increase of 264 from its previous update.

The agency listed 511 hospitalizations and three confirmed measles-associated deaths. Unvaccinated people and those whose vaccination status was unknown accounted for 96% of cases.

candidates.summary: Binance said it had replenished 90% of the cryptocurrency assets stolen in its recent hack. The exchange said the remaining assets were less-liquid tokens that could take longer to obtain in the required quantities.
candidates.title: Binance says 90% of stolen assets replenished

candidates.summary: Iranian negotiators held talks in Doha with Qatari mediators about possible steps toward ending the Gulf conflict, according to a source briefed on the discussions. Separately, Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei ordered the armed forces to prepare for an immediate response to any U.S. or Israeli attack, according to Iranian state media.
candidates.title: Iranian negotiators meet Qatari mediators in Doha

candidates.summary: China's coast guard conducted what it described as routine law-enforcement patrols in waters east of Taiwan, state broadcaster CCTV reported. A coast guard spokesperson said China had strengthened its control of the waters during October and would continue increasing patrols. Taiwan rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims.
candidates.title: China reports coast guard patrols east of Taiwan

candidates.summary: Nigeria's disease-control agency said it was investigating two suspected Ebola cases in the country's northeast. The two people were isolated while officials conducted contact identification and laboratory testing. Authorities emphasized that the cases remained unconfirmed and did not say whether they were linked to Nigeria's previously confirmed case.
candidates.title: Nigeria investigates two suspected Ebola cases

candidates.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service said the United States had warned it through established channels about preparations for a possible terrorist attack in Moscow. The U.S. Embassy separately warned of a credible threat of a mass-casualty event at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve. Russian authorities temporarily closed the complex and restricted access to its park.
candidates.title: U.S. warns Russia of possible Moscow attack

candidates.summary: Foreign ministers from the Group of 20 ended their Atlanta meeting without a joint statement amid divisions over Ukraine, the Iran conflict and other issues. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was reviewing Turkish and Indian proposals for a limited Black Sea ceasefire covering grain and some energy shipments. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said Russia had not shown willingness to proceed.
candidates.title: G20 meeting ends without consensus as Black Sea proposals circulate

candidates.summary: Governments at the COP17 biodiversity conference adopted the Yerevan Pathway, acknowledging that progress toward 2030 nature-protection targets was insufficient and agreeing to accelerate work on harmful subsidies, financing and national spending. Delegates did not resolve the broader funding shortfall and agreed that COP18 would be held in Quito, Ecuador, in 2028.
candidates.title: COP17 adopts pathway to accelerate biodiversity action

candidates.summary: Virginia and the District of Columbia filed a federal lawsuit seeking to block construction of the Trump administration's proposed 250-foot memorial arch near Arlington National Cemetery. They alleged that the project bypassed legal review requirements and would disrupt traffic, emergency services and the environment. The administration said construction could begin as early as the following week, but no court order had halted or approved it.
candidates.title: Virginia and D.C. sue to block proposed Trump arch
candidates.geography: Washington, D.C., and Virginia, United States

candidates.summary: A federal judge dismissed with prejudice President Donald Trump's second attempt to sue The Wall Street Journal over reporting about his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. The judge found that the amended complaint again failed to plausibly allege actual malice, citing the newspaper's investigation and efforts to seek comment. The ruling prevents the case from being refiled in that court.
candidates.title: Judge dismisses Trump's Wall Street Journal lawsuit with prejudice

candidates.summary: French police used tear gas and clashed with some demonstrators during a third consecutive weekend of nationwide protests over living costs, inequality, public services and policing. The Interior Ministry estimated turnout at 320,000 nationwide, including about 70,000 in Paris. Most demonstrations were peaceful, but clashes were reported in Paris, Marseille and other cities.
candidates.title: Police clash with protesters during nationwide French demonstrations

candidates.summary: Seven core OPEC+ producers reached an agreement in principle to leave their December oil-output targets unchanged, three people familiar with the discussions told Reuters. The provisional position was expected to be considered at an online meeting on November 1 and had not yet become a final group decision.
candidates.title: OPEC+ producers provisionally agree to hold December targets steady

candidates.summary: Several thousand housing protesters gathered in Lisbon's Rossio Square to demand that Portugal's government withdraw a bill that would make evictions easier and end rent caps on new leases. Prime Minister Luis Montenegro had ruled out withdrawing the bill but said amendments could be considered before its final parliamentary vote.
candidates.title: Lisbon protesters demand withdrawal of rental bill

candidates.summary: The U.N. human-rights chief disclosed that Yemeni employee Mohammad el Shami had died while held by the Houthis and called for an independent investigation. El Shami had been detained since June 2024; his family was informed only recently that he had died more than a month earlier and was given no explanation. The Houthis did not immediately comment.
candidates.title: U.N. discloses staff member's death in Houthi custody

candidates.summary: Russia agreed to work with Ghana on developing a 2,000-megawatt nuclear power plant following talks at the Russia-Africa Summit, Ghanaian Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa said. He also announced plans for deeper defense, agricultural and educational cooperation. The announcement did not provide a construction schedule or financing terms.
candidates.title: Ghana announces Russian cooperation on proposed nuclear plant

candidates.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said President Donald Trump agreed during a phone call to grant an immediate visa to the mother of a 15-year-old Ghanaian immigrant who was fatally shot in the Bronx on October 29. The mayor's office did not specify the visa category, and the White House had not independently confirmed the decision when local reporting was published.
candidates.title: Mamdani says Trump agreed to visa for slain teen's mother

candidates.summary: Alaska's Republican-led state government urged a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit filed at President Donald Trump's direction concerning the state's Senate election. The suit sought to prevent certification of a possible Democratic victory. State attorneys described the demand to set aside ballots as meritless and said the requested action was not possible under Alaska's election procedures.
candidates.title: Alaska asks judge to dismiss federal election lawsuit
